item.title: Angry crowd confronts Metrobloks over proposed data center
item.description: Over 70 people attended a public meeting to express their concerns over Metrobloks' proposed $500 million data center in the Martindale-Brightwood neighborhood, with some citing environmental pollution as a major concern.

item.title: First US-made Subaru hybrid rolls off Lafayette assembly line
item.description: Subaru of Indiana Automotive has begun hybrid production of the 2026 Forester Hybrid Premium, with all Forester models sold in the U.S. now assembled at the Lafayette, Ind. facility.

item.title: Westfield police check video after fights at Grand Park
item.description: Westfield Police Department investigators are reviewing video footage to identify people involved in several separate fights that happened Sunday afternoon during a kids' football event at the Grand Park Sports Campus.

item.title: Pedestrian killed in hit-and-run crash on North Shadeland Avenue
item.description: A pedestrian was killed in a hit-and-run crash Monday night on North Shadeland Avenue in Indianapolis, police said.

item.title: Man sentenced to 106 years in prison for crime spree
item.description: Terri Young-Moses was sentenced to 106 years in prison for the murder of Dezmond King and several other crimes that took place in 2021.

item.title: Indiana House clears bill to relocate casino to new county
item.description: House Bill 1038, which would allow four counties to bid for the relocation of the Rising Sun casino, has passed the House and is now awaiting Senate approval.

item.title: Body of missing Fishers teen Hailey Buzbee found in Ohio; suspect appears in court
item.description: 17-year-old Hailey Buzbee's remains were found in Perry County, Ohio, and Tyler Thomas, the primary suspect in her disappearance, has been charged with felony pandering and tampering with evidence.

item.title: Pat Knight, son of Bob Knight, resigns as Marian head basketball coach

item.title: Indiana keeps bucking marijuana legalization, tightening related laws instead
item.description: Despite President Trump's executive order to reclassify marijuana as a less-dangerous drug, Indiana's Republican-dominated state Legislature is advancing proposals to tighten laws on delta-8 products and crack down on marijuana advertisements, while advocates for legalization are pushing for the establishment of a state cannabis commission.
